answers.rationale: The helper must sit on the interface where client broadcasts arrive.

answers.answer_text: Point the helper to 10.10.99.255 on G0/1
answers.rationale: The interface is still wrong, and a unicast to the server is preferred.

answers.answer_text: Add ip helper-address 10.10.20.1 on G0/1
answers.rationale: 10.10.20.1 is the router itself, not the DHCP server.

answers.answer_text: Configure ip address dhcp on G0/0
answers.rationale: That would make the gateway interface a DHCP client and remove its static address.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which DSCP marking is recommended for voice bearer (RTP) traffic so that it can be placed in a low-latency priority queue?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Voice needs low delay, jitter and loss, so it is marked Expedited Forwarding (EF, DSCP 46) and served by a priority queue such as LLQ. On an 802.1Q trunk the matching Layer 2 marking is CoS 5. AF classes suit data or video that can tolerate some delay, and CS6 is reserved for network control traffic such as routing protocols.

answers.answer_text: AF41 (DSCP 34)
answers.rationale: AF41 is typically used for interactive video, not voice bearer traffic.

answers.answer_text: CS6 (DSCP 48)
answers.rationale: CS6 is reserved for network control traffic such as routing updates.

answers.answer_text: Default (DSCP 0)
answers.rationale: DSCP 0 is best effort and receives no priority treatment.

answers.answer_text: EF (DSCP 46)
answers.rationale: EF is the standard marking for voice and maps to the priority queue.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Three packets in the same queue are marked AF31, AF32 and AF33. As the queue fills and congestion avoidance (WRED) starts discarding, which marking is the most likely to be dropped first?
ccna-200-301.explanation: In AFxy, x is the class (the queue) and y is the drop precedence from 1 (low) to 3 (high). Within the same class, packets with a higher drop precedence are discarded earlier by WRED. AF33 is therefore dropped before AF32, and AF32 before AF31.

answers.answer_text: AF31
answers.rationale: AF31 has the lowest drop precedence in class 3, so it is protected longest.

answers.answer_text: AF32
answers.rationale: AF32 has medium drop precedence and is dropped after AF33.

answers.answer_text: AF33
answers.rationale: Its drop precedence of 3 is the highest in the class.

answers.answer_text: Equal odds for the three
answers.rationale: The second digit exists precisely to give different drop chances.

ccna-200-301.scenario: A branch router connects to a provider through a 1 Gbps Ethernet handoff, but the contract allows 200 Mbps. The provider polices traffic above 200 Mbps, and users see TCP retransmissions during bursts.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which QoS tool should the branch apply outbound to stay within the contract without losing the bursts?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Shaping and policing both enforce a rate. Policing drops or re-marks the excess immediately, which is what the provider does here. Shaping buffers the excess and sends it later, smoothing bursts down to the contracted rate at the cost of some delay; it is applied outbound, typically on the customer side facing a policed provider.

answers.answer_text: Policing at 200 Mbps
answers.rationale: Policing would drop the excess on the branch side, causing the same losses.

answers.answer_text: Shaping at 200 Mbps
answers.rationale: Shaping delays the excess instead of dropping it, matching the contract rate.

answers.answer_text: Marking with CoS 5
answers.rationale: Marking labels traffic but does not limit its rate.

answers.answer_text: Classification with NBAR
answers.rationale: Classification identifies traffic but does not control the sending rate.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
An administrator is preparing SW1 for SSH access:
SW1(config)# hostname SW1
SW1(config)# crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048
% Please define a domain-name first.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which command must be entered before the RSA keys can be generated?
ccna-200-301.explanation: IOS names the RSA key pair after the hostname and the domain name, so both must be set first (a hostname other than the default and an ip domain-name). The full SSH setup is: hostname, ip domain-name, crypto key generate rsa, a local username, then login local and transport input ssh on the VTY lines; ip ssh version 2 is recommended.

answers.answer_text: ip domain-name corp.local
answers.rationale: The key pair name uses the domain name, which is missing here.

answers.answer_text: ip ssh version 2
answers.rationale: This selects the SSH version but does not satisfy the key prerequisite.

answers.answer_text: username admin secret S3cr3t
answers.rationale: A local user is needed for login, not for generating keys.

answers.answer_text: transport input ssh
answers.rationale: This is a VTY line command applied after the keys exist.

ccna-200-301.question_text: The VTY lines of a router are configured with login local and transport input ssh. Which command creates a credential that these lines will accept?
ccna-200-301.explanation: login local tells the lines to check the username and password against the local user database, which is built with username <name> secret <password>. A password set under the line is used by plain login, and enable secret protects privileged EXEC mode. SSH logins need a username, which is another reason to use the local database.

answers.answer_text: enable secret Adm1n!
answers.rationale: This protects privileged EXEC mode, not the VTY login.

answers.answer_text: username netops secret Adm1n!
answers.rationale: It adds a user to the local database checked by login local.

answers.answer_text: password Adm1n! under line vty
answers.rationale: A line password is used by the login command, not by login local.

answers.answer_text: service password-encryption
answers.rationale: This obscures stored passwords but creates no account.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which command shows whether SSH is enabled on a Cisco router and which SSH version it runs?
ccna-200-301.explanation: show ip ssh displays whether SSH is enabled, the version in use (for example 2.0), the authentication timeout and retries. show ssh lists the active SSH sessions, and show crypto key mypubkey rsa displays the generated keys. These commands are the quick way to confirm an SSH setup.

answers.answer_text: show users
answers.rationale: This lists logged-in users per line, not the SSH status or version.

answers.answer_text: show crypto key mypubkey rsa
answers.rationale: This displays the RSA public keys, not the SSH version in use.

answers.answer_text: show ip interface brief
answers.rationale: This shows interface addresses and status, not SSH.

answers.answer_text: show ip ssh
answers.rationale: It reports whether SSH is enabled and its version.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which transport protocol and port does a TFTP server listen on?
ccna-200-301.explanation: TFTP is a minimal file transfer protocol that runs over UDP port 69, with no authentication and no directory listing; reliability comes from TFTP's own simple acknowledgments. FTP runs over TCP, using port 21 for control and port 20 for data in active mode, and requires a login.

answers.answer_text: TCP port 69
answers.rationale: Port 69 is right, but TFTP uses UDP, not TCP.

answers.answer_text: UDP port 69
answers.rationale: TFTP servers listen on UDP 69.

answers.answer_text: TCP port 21
answers.rationale: TCP 21 is the FTP control port.

answers.answer_text: UDP port 21
answers.rationale: Port 21 belongs to FTP, which uses TCP.

ccna-200-301.scenario: A new IOS image is stored on TFTP server 10.0.0.25. The router can reach the server and has enough free space in flash.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which privileged EXEC command starts copying the image onto the router?
ccna-200-301.explanation: The copy command reads as copy <source> <destination>, so copy tftp: flash: pulls a file from a TFTP server into flash; IOS then prompts for the server address and file names. After the copy, verify the file with show flash: and point the router at it with boot system before reloading.

answers.answer_text: copy flash: tftp:
answers.rationale: This copies from flash to the server, the wrong direction.

answers.answer_text: copy running-config tftp:
answers.rationale: This backs up the configuration; it does not fetch an image.

answers.answer_text: copy tftp: flash:
answers.rationale: The source is the TFTP server and the destination is flash.

answers.answer_text: copy tftp: running-config
answers.rationale: This merges a configuration file into RAM; it is not used for images.

ccna-200-301.question_text: An engineer must transfer an IOS image to a router from a file server that requires a username and password. Which protocol fits, and which port carries its control connection?
ccna-200-301.explanation: TFTP has no authentication, so a server that requires credentials points to FTP. FTP uses TCP: port 21 carries the control connection (login and commands) and port 20 carries data in active mode. On IOS the credentials can be given with ip ftp username and ip ftp password or inside the URL.

answers.answer_text: FTP, TCP port 21
answers.rationale: FTP supports logins and uses TCP 21 for its control channel.

answers.answer_text: FTP, TCP port 20
answers.rationale: Port 20 carries FTP data in active mode, not the control connection.

answers.answer_text: TFTP, UDP port 69
answers.rationale: TFTP cannot authenticate users, so it does not fit this server.

answers.answer_text: TFTP, TCP port 69
answers.rationale: TFTP does not authenticate users and runs over UDP.

ccna-200-301.question_text: An attacker runs a small program that takes advantage of an unpatched buffer overflow in a web server to execute code on it. In security terminology, what is that program?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A vulnerability is the weakness itself (here, the unpatched buffer overflow). An exploit is the code or technique that uses that weakness, and a threat is the potential danger that someone uses an exploit against the vulnerability. Mitigation techniques reduce the risk, for example by patching.

answers.answer_text: A threat
answers.rationale: A threat is the potential for an attacker to cause harm, not the tool used to do it.

answers.answer_text: An exploit
answers.rationale: An exploit is the code or method that takes advantage of a vulnerability.

answers.answer_text: A vulnerability
answers.rationale: The vulnerability is the unpatched buffer overflow, not the program that abuses it.

answers.answer_text: A mitigation
answers.rationale: A mitigation reduces risk, such as applying the patch; it does not attack the system.

ccna-200-301.scenario: An employee receives a phone call from someone claiming to work at the IT help desk. The caller asks for the employee's VPN password to "fix an account problem".
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which type of social engineering attack is this?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Vishing (voice phishing) uses phone calls or voice messages to trick victims into revealing information. Smishing uses SMS text messages, whaling targets senior executives, and pharming redirects users to fake websites, often by tampering with DNS. User awareness training helps staff recognize these attempts.

answers.answer_text: Smishing
answers.rationale: Smishing is phishing carried out through SMS text messages, not voice calls.

answers.answer_text: Pharming
answers.rationale: Pharming redirects users to a fraudulent website, for example through DNS poisoning.

answers.answer_text: Whaling
answers.rationale: Whaling targets high-profile executives; here the target is an ordinary employee called by phone.

answers.answer_text: Vishing
answers.rationale: Vishing is voice phishing: the attacker uses a phone call to obtain the password.

ccna-200-301.scenario: Every quarter, the security team sends fake phishing emails to staff, records who clicks the link, and shows those users a short page explaining the warning signs they missed.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which security program element does this activity belong to?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A security program combines user awareness, user training and physical access control. User awareness keeps people alert to threats in their daily work, and simulated phishing campaigns are a classic example. Technical controls such as AAA or password policies do not change how users react to a deceptive email.

answers.answer_text: User awareness program
answers.rationale: Simulated phishing that teaches users to spot real attacks is a user awareness activity.

answers.answer_text: Physical access control
answers.rationale: Physical access control protects rooms and equipment with badges, locks or guards, not email behavior.

answers.answer_text: AAA accounting
answers.rationale: AAA accounting logs what authenticated users do on network devices; it does not educate staff.

answers.answer_text: Password complexity policy
answers.rationale: A complexity policy governs how passwords are built, not how users react to phishing.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Why does a security program still require physical access control for routers that already use strong enable secrets and SSH?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Anyone who can reach the console port and power-cycle a Cisco router can interrupt the boot process, change the configuration register and bypass the startup configuration, which is the documented password recovery procedure. Strong passwords do not stop this. Locked rooms, racks and badge access are therefore part of the security program.

answers.answer_text: Console traffic is sent in clear text across the LAN
answers.rationale: The console is a local serial connection; it does not cross the LAN.

answers.answer_text: Enable secrets are erased when the router reloads
answers.rationale: A saved enable secret stays in the startup configuration across reloads.

answers.answer_text: Console access allows password recovery at boot time
answers.rationale: With physical access, an attacker can interrupt the boot and bypass the configured passwords.

answers.answer_text: SSH sessions must be approved by someone at the console
answers.rationale: IOS has no such approval step; SSH authenticates the user directly.

ccna-200-301.topic: Device access control with local passwords
ccna-200-301.scenario:
R1 has the following lines in its running configuration:

hostname R1
enable password Cisco123
enable secret Adm!n2026
ccna-200-301.question_text: An administrator types enable on R1. Which password is accepted to enter privileged EXEC mode?
ccna-200-301.explanation: When both enable password and enable secret are configured, IOS uses the enable secret and ignores the enable password. The enable secret is stored as a one-way hash, while enable password is plain text (or weak type 7 with service password-encryption). Best practice is to configure only enable secret.

answers.answer_text: Cisco123, because it is configured first
answers.rationale: The order of the lines does not matter; enable secret overrides enable password.

answers.answer_text: Either one, because both are configured
answers.rationale: IOS does not accept both; once enable secret exists, enable password is ignored.

answers.answer_text: Adm!n2026, as the enable secret wins
answers.rationale: When both exist, IOS checks the enable secret and ignores the enable password.

answers.answer_text: Neither one, because the commands conflict
answers.rationale: The two commands can coexist; IOS simply uses the enable secret.

ccna-200-301.topic: Device access control with local passwords
ccna-200-301.scenario:
The console line of a switch is configured as follows:

line con 0
 password C0nsole!
 exec-timeout 5 0
ccna-200-301.question_text: A technician connects to the console port and reaches the user EXEC prompt without being asked for a password. What is the cause?
ccna-200-301.explanation: The password command only defines the line password; the login command tells IOS to actually prompt for it. By default the console line has no login, so without that command the password is never checked. Use login (line password) or login local (local username database) under line con 0.

answers.answer_text: The login command is missing under line con 0
answers.rationale: Without login, IOS does not prompt for the line password even though one is set.

answers.answer_text: service password-encryption is not enabled
answers.rationale: That command only obfuscates stored passwords; it does not enable the prompt.

answers.answer_text: transport input is missing under line con 0
answers.rationale: transport input controls protocols on vty lines; it has no effect on console authentication.

answers.answer_text: The exec-timeout value disables authentication
answers.rationale: exec-timeout 5 0 only logs out an idle session after five minutes.

ccna-200-301.topic: Device access control with local passwords
ccna-200-301.question_text: What does the global configuration command service password-encryption do?
ccna-200-301.explanation: service password-encryption converts clear-text passwords in the configuration (line passwords, enable password, username password) to type 7, which only hides them from casual viewing. It does not touch enable secret or username secret, which are already hashed. It also does nothing for traffic on the wire, so SSH is still needed instead of Telnet.

answers.answer_text: It converts the enable secret into a type 7 string
answers.rationale: The enable secret is already hashed and is left unchanged by this command.

answers.answer_text: It encrypts Telnet sessions to the device
answers.rationale: It affects the stored configuration, not traffic; Telnet stays in clear text.

answers.answer_text: It hashes line passwords with SHA-256 (type 8)
answers.rationale: The result is reversible type 7, not a type 8 hash.

answers.answer_text: It hides plaintext config passwords as type 7
answers.rationale: Plaintext passwords such as line passwords are shown as password 7 followed by an obfuscated string.

ccna-200-301.question_text: A password policy requires at least 10 characters for every password configured on a router. Which IOS global configuration command enforces this?
ccna-200-301.explanation: security passwords min-length sets the minimum length that IOS accepts for new passwords such as enable secret, line and username passwords. Passwords already configured are not changed, but shorter new ones are rejected. This supports a password policy alongside complexity, rotation and multifactor authentication.

answers.answer_text: password-policy length 10
answers.rationale: This is not a valid IOS global configuration command.

answers.answer_text: security passwords min-length 10
answers.rationale: This command makes IOS reject new passwords shorter than 10 characters.

answers.answer_text: service password-length 10
answers.rationale: No such service command exists; it mixes up service password-encryption.

answers.answer_text: login block-for 10
answers.rationale: login block-for blocks logins after failed attempts; it does not set a length.

ccna-200-301.question_text: To open the server room, an engineer places a finger on a reader and then types a six-digit PIN on a keypad. Which authentication factors are combined?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Authentication factors are something you know (password, PIN), something you have (token, smart card, phone) and something you are (biometrics such as a fingerprint). Combining two different categories is multifactor authentication. Two items from the same category, such as two passwords, are not.

answers.answer_text: Something you are and something you know
answers.rationale: The fingerprint is a biometric (are) and the PIN is a secret (know).

answers.answer_text: Something you have and something you know
answers.rationale: No token or card is used; the finger is a biometric, not a possession.

answers.answer_text: Something you know, used twice
answers.rationale: A fingerprint is not a memorized secret.

answers.answer_text: Something you are and something you have
answers.rationale: The PIN is memorized, so it is a knowledge factor, not a possession factor.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which IPsec protocol can provide confidentiality by encrypting the user data it carries?
ccna-200-301.explanation: IPsec has two security protocols: AH provides authentication and integrity but no encryption, while ESP provides encryption plus authentication and integrity. IKE negotiates keys and security associations but does not carry user traffic. Because it offers confidentiality, ESP is the protocol used in practically all IPsec VPNs.

answers.answer_text: AH (Authentication Header)
answers.rationale: AH authenticates and protects integrity but does not encrypt the payload.

answers.answer_text: IKE (Internet Key Exchange)
answers.rationale: IKE negotiates keys and SAs; it does not carry user data.

answers.answer_text: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload)
answers.rationale: ESP encrypts the payload and can also authenticate it.

answers.answer_text: GRE (Generic Routing Encapsulation)
answers.rationale: GRE is a tunneling protocol without encryption and is not part of IPsec.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Before two IPsec peers can protect traffic, which protocol do they use to authenticate each other and negotiate security associations and keys?
ccna-200-301.explanation: IKE (Internet Key Exchange, UDP port 500) authenticates the peers, for example with a pre-shared key or certificates, and agrees on algorithms and keys. The resulting security associations are then used by ESP or AH to protect the data. Without a successful IKE negotiation, no traffic is encrypted.

answers.answer_text: ESP
answers.rationale: ESP protects data using the SAs that are negotiated beforehand.

answers.answer_text: IKE
answers.rationale: IKE authenticates the peers and negotiates the SAs and keys.

answers.answer_text: AH
answers.rationale: AH protects packet integrity once SAs exist; it does not negotiate them.

answers.answer_text: TLS
answers.rationale: TLS secures sessions such as HTTPS or SSL VPNs, not IPsec SA negotiation.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which characteristic describes a remote-access VPN rather than a site-to-site VPN?
ccna-200-301.explanation: In a remote-access VPN, VPN client software on a laptop or phone (for example Cisco Secure Client) builds a tunnel on demand to a VPN gateway. In a site-to-site VPN, two gateways such as routers or firewalls keep a tunnel between their LANs, and the end hosts send normal unencrypted traffic that the gateways protect.

answers.answer_text: Two routers keep a permanent tunnel between LANs
answers.rationale: A permanent gateway-to-gateway tunnel is the site-to-site model.

answers.answer_text: Hosts send clear traffic that a gateway encrypts
answers.rationale: Gateways encrypting on behalf of hosts describes site-to-site VPNs.

answers.answer_text: It requires an MPLS provider between the sites
answers.rationale: VPNs over the Internet need no MPLS service; MPLS VPN is a different technology.

answers.answer_text: Client software on the device builds the tunnel
answers.rationale: Remote-access VPNs rely on a client on the user's device that connects on demand.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which access-list number creates a numbered standard IPv4 ACL?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Numbered standard IPv4 ACLs use 1 to 99 and the expanded range 1300 to 1999. Numbered extended IPv4 ACLs use 100 to 199 and the expanded range 2000 to 2699. The number alone tells IOS which syntax and matching options to expect.

answers.rationale: 150 is in 100 to 199, the extended ACL range.
2050 is in 2000 to 2699, the expanded extended ACL range.
199 is the last number of the extended range 100 to 199.
1350 falls in 1300 to 1999, the expanded standard ACL range.

ccna-200-301.question_text: An ACL entry must match every address in 172.16.32.0/20. Which wildcard mask must follow 172.16.32.0 in the entry?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A wildcard mask is the inverse of the subnet mask: subtract each octet of the mask from 255. A /20 mask is 255.255.240.0, so the wildcard is 0.0.15.255. Bits set to 0 must match and bits set to 1 are ignored, which covers 172.16.32.0 to 172.16.47.255.

answers.rationale: 0.0.31.255 is the wildcard of a /19, which would match twice as many addresses.
This is the subnet mask, not the wildcard mask that ACLs expect.
16 is the block size; the wildcard octet is the block size minus 1.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
A router has this configuration:

access-list 25 deny host 192.168.5.10
access-list 25 permit 192.168.5.0 0.0.0.255
!
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 ip access-group 25 out
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which statement about packets routed out of G0/1 is correct?
ccna-200-301.explanation: IOS checks ACL entries from top to bottom and stops at the first match. Host 192.168.5.10 matches the first deny, other 192.168.5.0/24 hosts match the permit, and any other source matches nothing and is dropped by the implicit deny any at the end of every ACL. To let other sources through, a permit any entry must be added at the end.

answers.answer_text: Packets from 192.168.6.20 are dropped by the implicit deny
answers.rationale: 192.168.6.20 matches neither entry, so the implicit deny any drops it.

answers.answer_text: Packets from 192.168.5.10 are permitted by the second entry
answers.rationale: The first entry already matches and denies this host; later entries are not checked.

answers.answer_text: Packets from 192.168.6.20 pass since the ACL has no deny for them
answers.rationale: Unmatched packets are not permitted; the implicit deny drops them.

answers.answer_text: Packets from 192.168.5.11 are dropped by the first entry
answers.rationale: The first entry matches host 192.168.5.10 alone; .11 matches the permit.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Why is a standard IPv4 ACL normally placed as close as possible to the destination?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A standard ACL matches only the source address, so it cannot tell which destination a packet is going to. Applied near the source, it would drop that source's traffic to every destination, not just the protected one. Extended ACLs match source, destination, protocol and ports, so they are placed near the source to discard unwanted traffic early.

answers.answer_text: It filters on TCP and UDP port numbers
answers.rationale: Port filtering is a feature of extended ACLs, not standard ACLs.

answers.answer_text: It is checked after the routing table lookup
answers.rationale: Timing depends on in or out direction, not on the ACL type, and does not drive placement.

answers.answer_text: It matches the source only, so it would block too much
answers.rationale: Without a destination field, a standard ACL near the source would block traffic to every destination.

answers.answer_text: It uses less memory on routers that are close to servers
answers.rationale: Memory use does not depend on where the ACL is applied.

ccna-200-301.scenario: On R1, G0/0 connects to the user LAN 10.20.0.0/24 and G0/1 connects to the WAN toward a remote server. Extended ACL 110 already exists and denies Telnet from 10.20.0.0/24 to that server. It must be applied as close to the source as possible.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which configuration applies ACL 110 correctly?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Extended ACLs go near the source so unwanted packets are dropped before crossing the network. On R1, user packets enter through G0/0, so ip access-group 110 in on G0/0 filters them as soon as they arrive. The direction is always seen from the router: in means arriving on that interface, out means leaving it.

answers.answer_text: On G0/1: ip access-group 110 in
answers.rationale: Inbound on G0/1 checks traffic arriving from the WAN, not the users' outgoing traffic.

answers.answer_text: On G0/0: ip access-group 110 out
answers.rationale: Outbound on G0/0 checks traffic going to the LAN, so user packets to the server are not filtered.

answers.answer_text: On G0/0: ip access-group 110 in
answers.rationale: User packets enter R1 on G0/0, so inbound there is the closest point to the source.

answers.answer_text: On G0/1: ip access-class 110 out
answers.rationale: access-class applies an ACL to vty lines, not to a routed interface.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
R2# show access-lists 120
Extended IP access list 120
    10 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.20 eq 443 (57 matches)
    20 permit tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.20 eq 22
    30 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.20 (12 matches)
    40 permit ip any any (230 matches)
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which conclusion does this output support?
ccna-200-301.explanation: show access-lists displays a match counter per entry; an entry with no counter has not matched any packet since the counters were last cleared. Because of first-match processing, HTTPS packets stop at entry 10 and never reach entry 30. Entry 40 permits everything else, so the implicit deny is never reached in this ACL.

answers.answer_text: No SSH from 192.168.10.0/24 to 10.0.0.20 has matched so far
answers.rationale: Entry 20 shows no counter, so no SSH packet has matched it since the last clear.

answers.answer_text: Entry 30 has dropped 12 HTTPS packets sent to 10.0.0.20 so far
answers.rationale: HTTPS from that subnet matches entry 10 first, so it cannot reach entry 30.

answers.answer_text: The implicit deny has dropped 230 packets
answers.rationale: The 230 matches belong to entry 40, which permits the packets.

answers.answer_text: Entry 30 blocks other subnets from reaching 10.0.0.20
answers.rationale: Entry 30 matches 192.168.10.0/24 as the source; other subnets fall through to entry 40.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which command creates a named extended IPv4 ACL called BLOCK-FTP and enters its configuration mode?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Named ACLs are created with ip access-list standard|extended name, which opens a sub-mode where entries are added with sequence numbers. Named ACLs make it easy to insert or delete a single entry by its sequence number. The ACL is then applied with ip access-group BLOCK-FTP in or out on an interface.

answers.answer_text: access-list extended BLOCK-FTP
answers.rationale: The access-list command creates numbered ACLs and does not take a name.

answers.answer_text: ip access-list BLOCK-FTP extended
answers.rationale: The type keyword must come before the name.

answers.answer_text: ip access-group BLOCK-FTP extended
answers.rationale: ip access-group applies an ACL to an interface; it does not create one.

answers.answer_text: ip access-list extended BLOCK-FTP
answers.rationale: This is the correct syntax and opens the named extended ACL sub-mode.

ccna-200-301.scenario: DHCP snooping is enabled for VLAN 30. Gi1/0/48, toward the company DHCP server, is trusted. A user plugs a home router into Gi1/0/12, an untrusted port, and the router starts answering DHCP requests.
ccna-200-301.question_text: What does the switch do with the DHCPOFFER messages arriving on Gi1/0/12?
ccna-200-301.explanation: DHCP snooping classifies ports as trusted or untrusted. Server messages such as DHCPOFFER and DHCPACK are accepted on trusted ports and dropped on untrusted ports, which stops rogue DHCP servers. Client messages on untrusted ports are still allowed and are used to build the binding table.

answers.answer_text: It forwards them and logs a warning
answers.rationale: Forwarding them would let the rogue server hand out addresses.

answers.answer_text: It drops them because the port is untrusted
answers.rationale: DHCP server messages are discarded on untrusted ports.

answers.answer_text: It forwards them after removing option 82
answers.rationale: Option 82 handling does not make server messages acceptable on an untrusted port.

answers.answer_text: It moves Gi1/0/12 into VLAN 1
answers.rationale: DHCP snooping does not change the VLAN assignment of a port.

ccna-200-301.scenario: DHCP snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection are enabled on VLAN 40. PCs that obtain addresses through DHCP work normally. A printer with a manually configured static IP address, on an untrusted port, cannot communicate, and the switch logs dropped ARP packets from it.
ccna-200-301.question_text: What is the most likely cause?
ccna-200-301.explanation: On untrusted ports, DAI compares the sender IP and MAC of each ARP message with the DHCP snooping binding table. A host with a static address never went through DHCP, so it has no binding and its ARP messages are dropped. The fix is an ARP ACL for that host (or a static binding), not disabling DAI.

answers.answer_text: The printer port is a DHCP snooping trusted port
answers.rationale: The scenario says the port is untrusted, and DHCP trust does not cause ARP drops.

answers.answer_text: The printer exceeds the port-security maximum
answers.rationale: A port-security violation would be logged as such, not as dropped ARP packets.

answers.answer_text: DAI requires hosts to send gratuitous ARP
answers.rationale: DAI does not require gratuitous ARP; it validates ARP against known bindings.

answers.answer_text: There is no snooping binding for its IP and MAC
answers.rationale: A static host has no DHCP snooping binding, so DAI drops its ARP messages.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
interface GigabitEthernet0/5
 switchport mode access
 switchport port-security
 switchport port-security maximum 1
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky
 switchport port-security violation restrict
 switchport port-security mac-address sticky 0011.2233.4455
ccna-200-301.question_text: A user adds a small unmanaged switch on Gi0/5 and connects a laptop with MAC 00aa.bbcc.ddee next to the host 0011.2233.4455. What happens to the laptop's frames?
ccna-200-301.explanation: With maximum 1 and one sticky MAC already learned, any other source MAC is a violation. Restrict mode drops the offending frames, increments the violation counter and sends syslog and SNMP messages while the port stays up for the authorized host. Protect drops silently, and shutdown (the default) puts the port in err-disabled state.

answers.answer_text: Dropped, with a log message and a violation count
answers.rationale: Restrict drops the frames, logs the event and increments the counter; the port stays up.

answers.answer_text: Dropped silently, with the violation count unchanged
answers.rationale: That is protect mode, which does not log or count violations.

answers.answer_text: The port goes err-disabled and stops forwarding
answers.rationale: That is shutdown mode, but this port is configured with restrict.

answers.answer_text: The new MAC replaces the sticky entry in the config
answers.rationale: A sticky MAC is not replaced by a new source; the new MAC causes a violation.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which transport protocol and port does TACACS+ use?
ccna-200-301.explanation: TACACS+ runs over TCP port 49. RADIUS runs over UDP, on ports 1812 (authentication) and 1813 (accounting), or the older 1645 and 1646. Knowing these ports helps when permitting AAA traffic through ACLs or firewalls.

answers.answer_text: UDP 1812
answers.rationale: UDP 1812 is the RADIUS authentication port.

answers.answer_text: UDP 49
answers.rationale: TACACS+ uses port 49 but over TCP, not UDP.

answers.answer_text: TCP 49
answers.rationale: TACACS+ uses TCP port 49 for reliable delivery.

answers.answer_text: TCP 1812
answers.rationale: 1812 is a RADIUS port, and RADIUS uses UDP.

ccna-200-301.question_text: An audit requires that usernames and authorization data exchanged with the AAA server are not readable on the wire. How do RADIUS and TACACS+ compare on this point?
ccna-200-301.explanation: TACACS+ encrypts the entire body of its packets, leaving only the header in clear text. RADIUS hides the user password but sends other attributes, such as the username and authorization data, in clear text. This is one reason TACACS+ is often chosen for device administration.

answers.answer_text: RADIUS encrypts the whole body; TACACS+ hides the password
answers.rationale: This reverses the two protocols.

answers.answer_text: Both protocols encrypt the entire packet body
answers.rationale: RADIUS protects the password attribute, not the whole body.

answers.answer_text: Both protocols send every field in clear text
answers.rationale: Both protect at least the password; TACACS+ encrypts the whole body.

answers.answer_text: TACACS+ encrypts the body; RADIUS hides the password
answers.rationale: TACACS+ encrypts the full payload, while RADIUS protects only the password attribute.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Junior administrators must be able to run show commands on routers but be refused when they type configure terminal, with each command checked against a central server. Which protocol is best suited, and why?
ccna-200-301.explanation: TACACS+ separates authentication, authorization and accounting into distinct exchanges, so the router can ask the server to authorize each command. RADIUS combines authentication and authorization in one response, which suits network access (802.1X, VPN) better than per-command control. RADIUS is the open IETF standard, while TACACS+ was developed by Cisco.

answers.answer_text: RADIUS, as it merges authentication with authorization
answers.rationale: Merging the two steps prevents separate per-command authorization.

answers.answer_text: TACACS+, as it authorizes separately for each command
answers.rationale: TACACS+ separates the AAA functions and supports command authorization.

answers.answer_text: RADIUS, as it uses TCP for reliable delivery
answers.rationale: RADIUS uses UDP; TCP is used by TACACS+.

answers.answer_text: TACACS+, as it is the open IETF access standard
answers.rationale: RADIUS is the IETF standard; TACACS+ was developed by Cisco.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which encryption and integrity protocol is required by WPA2?
ccna-200-301.explanation: WPA2 requires CCMP, which uses AES for encryption and CBC-MAC for integrity. The original WPA used TKIP, built on the RC4 cipher, as a temporary fix for WEP. WPA3 uses GCMP for its higher security modes.

answers.answer_text: CCMP, based on AES
answers.rationale: CCMP with AES is the mandatory WPA2 protocol.

answers.answer_text: TKIP, based on RC4
answers.rationale: TKIP was introduced with the original WPA and is deprecated.

answers.answer_text: WEP, with a 104-bit key
answers.rationale: WEP is the broken legacy method that WPA and WPA2 replaced.

answers.answer_text: GCMP-256, based on AES
answers.rationale: GCMP-256 is associated with WPA3, not required by WPA2.

ccna-200-301.question_text: A WPA2-Enterprise WLAN uses a Cisco WLC and a RADIUS server, and the laptops run an 802.1X client. Which 802.1X role does the WLC play?
ccna-200-301.explanation: 802.1X defines three roles: the supplicant (the client device), the authenticator (the WLC or switch that controls access) and the authentication server (usually RADIUS). The authenticator relays EAP messages between the supplicant and the server and opens access only after a successful authentication.

answers.answer_text: Supplicant
answers.rationale: The supplicant is the laptop's 802.1X client.

answers.answer_text: Authentication server
answers.rationale: The RADIUS server is the authentication server.

answers.answer_text: Authenticator
answers.rationale: The WLC controls access and relays EAP between client and RADIUS server.

answers.answer_text: Certificate authority
answers.rationale: A CA issues certificates and is not one of the three 802.1X roles.

ccna-200-301.topic: WLAN with WPA2 PSK in the GUI
ccna-200-301.question_text: On a Cisco AireOS WLC GUI, where does an administrator start creating a new WLAN, before entering the profile name and SSID?
ccna-200-301.explanation: New WLANs are created from the WLANs tab by choosing Create New and clicking Go. The next page asks for the type, profile name, SSID and WLAN ID; after Apply, the WLAN edit page opens with its General, Security, QoS and Advanced tabs. The WLAN must also be enabled on the General tab.

answers.answer_text: CONTROLLER > Interfaces > New
answers.rationale: This creates a dynamic interface, which a WLAN can later be mapped to.

answers.answer_text: WLANs > Create New > Go
answers.rationale: This is where a new WLAN profile and SSID are defined.

answers.answer_text: WIRELESS > Access Points > Add
answers.rationale: The WIRELESS menu manages APs and radios, not WLAN creation.

answers.answer_text: SECURITY > AAA > RADIUS > New
answers.rationale: This adds a RADIUS server definition; it does not create a WLAN or its SSID.

ccna-200-301.topic: WLAN with WPA2 PSK in the GUI
ccna-200-301.scenario: A new WLAN named STAFF is open in the WLC GUI on the Security > Layer 2 tab. It must use WPA2 Personal with the strongest encryption that WPA2 offers.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which settings should be selected on this tab?
ccna-200-301.explanation: For WPA2 Personal, set Layer 2 Security to WPA+WPA2, check WPA2 Policy and select AES as the WPA2 encryption. TKIP is a legacy option, and WEP choices are insecure. The Authentication Key Management section of the same tab is then set to PSK with the passphrase.

answers.answer_text: Static WEP, with a 104-bit key
answers.rationale: Static WEP is not WPA2 and is easily cracked.

answers.answer_text: WPA+WPA2, WPA2 Policy with TKIP
answers.rationale: TKIP is the weaker legacy cipher; AES is the strongest WPA2 option.

answers.answer_text: 802.1X, with dynamic WEP keys
answers.rationale: This option uses WEP with a RADIUS server, not WPA2 Personal.

answers.answer_text: WPA+WPA2, WPA2 Policy with AES
answers.rationale: WPA+WPA2 with the WPA2 Policy and AES gives WPA2 with CCMP encryption.

ccna-200-301.topic: WLAN with WPA2 PSK in the GUI
ccna-200-301.question_text: A WLAN is set to WPA+WPA2 with WPA2 AES on the WLC. Users will join with the shared passphrase Brux3lles!Office. Which Authentication Key Management setting completes the configuration?
ccna-200-301.explanation: WPA2 Personal uses a pre-shared key, so PSK is enabled under Authentication Key Management. A typed passphrase uses the ASCII format and must be 8 to 63 characters; the HEX format expects exactly 64 hexadecimal digits. 802.1X key management would require a RADIUS server instead of a passphrase.

answers.answer_text: PSK enabled, ASCII format, passphrase entered
answers.rationale: A passphrase of letters and symbols is entered in ASCII format with PSK enabled.

answers.answer_text: 802.1X enabled, RADIUS server under AAA Servers
answers.rationale: 802.1X is WPA2 Enterprise and does not use a shared passphrase.

answers.answer_text: PSK enabled, PSK Format HEX, passphrase entered
answers.rationale: HEX expects 64 hexadecimal digits, not a text passphrase.

answers.answer_text: CCKM enabled, passphrase on the General tab
answers.rationale: CCKM is a fast roaming method for 802.1X, and the passphrase is not set on the General tab.

ccna-200-301.scenario: An automation script applies a new ACL template to 150 branch routers in a few minutes. The template contains a wrong wildcard mask, and the 150 routers now block a business application.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which lesson about network automation does this incident illustrate?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Automation brings speed and consistency: the same change is applied identically everywhere, which removes the random typos of manual CLI work. The flip side is that a mistake in the template is also applied consistently and just as fast. Automated workflows therefore include validation (lab tests, dry runs, peer review) and a rollback plan before a change is pushed to production.

answers.answer_text: Automation makes random per-device typos more likely than manual work
answers.rationale: Automation reduces random per-device typos; the problem here is one error copied everywhere.

answers.answer_text: A template error is replicated at scale, so templates need testing first
answers.rationale: Correct: automation applies a flawed template as fast and as consistently as a good one.

answers.answer_text: Changes pushed by a script cannot be rolled back on Cisco routers
answers.rationale: False: the same tool (or a saved configuration) can push the corrected or previous ACL.

answers.answer_text: The routers should have rejected the ACL because a script, not a person, sent it
answers.rationale: A router accepts a syntactically valid ACL whatever its source; it cannot judge the business intent.

ccna-200-301.question_text: A change that took a team six hours of manual CLI work on 80 switches now completes in ten minutes with an automation tool, with an identical result on every switch. Which pair of benefits does this show?
ccna-200-301.explanation: The main benefits of network automation are speed (many devices changed in minutes), consistency (the same configuration everywhere) and fewer human errors. Automation does not change how fast the hardware forwards traffic, and it does not remove the need for change control; it makes changes faster and more predictable.

answers.answer_text: Lower bandwidth use and stronger encryption on the switches
answers.rationale: Automation changes how configuration is deployed, not bandwidth use or encryption strength.

answers.answer_text: Less need for change approval and fewer devices to manage
answers.rationale: The number of switches is unchanged, and automated changes still go through change control.

answers.answer_text: Higher forwarding performance and lower latency on the switches
answers.rationale: Forwarding speed depends on the data plane hardware, not on how the configuration was entered.

answers.answer_text: Faster deployment and consistent configuration across devices
answers.rationale: Correct: ten minutes instead of six hours, with the same result on every switch.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which activity belongs to the management plane of a network device?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Device functions are grouped into three planes. The data plane forwards user traffic (MAC table, FIB lookups). The control plane builds the information used for forwarding (OSPF, STP, ARP). The management plane is how administrators and tools access and configure the device: SSH, Telnet, SNMP, syslog, NETCONF.

answers.answer_text: An administrator logs in with SSH to change the configuration
answers.rationale: Correct: remote administrative access such as SSH is a management plane function.

answers.answer_text: A router exchanges OSPF LSAs to build its routing table
answers.rationale: Routing protocol exchanges belong to the control plane.

answers.answer_text: A router sends a packet out an interface after a lookup in its FIB
answers.rationale: Forwarding user packets is the data plane.

answers.answer_text: A switch sends BPDUs to elect the spanning tree root bridge
answers.rationale: STP BPDUs build the loop-free topology, a control plane function.

ccna-200-301.question_text: In a traditional network without a controller, how is the control plane organized?
ccna-200-301.explanation: In a traditional network the control plane is distributed: every router and switch runs its own protocols (OSPF, STP, ARP) and makes its own forwarding decisions, and each device is configured one by one. A controller-based design centralizes part or all of the control and management functions in a controller, which then programs the devices through southbound interfaces.

answers.answer_text: A central controller computes paths and programs each device
answers.rationale: This describes a controller-based (SDN) design, not a traditional one.

answers.answer_text: The core switches compute routes and send them to access switches
answers.rationale: Core devices do not compute routes on behalf of other devices; each one runs its own protocols.

answers.answer_text: Each device runs its own control plane and builds its own tables
answers.rationale: Correct: the control plane is distributed across the devices.

answers.answer_text: The management plane computes routes from the SNMP data it polls
answers.rationale: SNMP is used for monitoring and management; it does not compute routes.

ccna-200-301.scenario: A Python script sends HTTPS REST requests to Cisco Catalyst Center to retrieve the device inventory. Catalyst Center then uses NETCONF to push a configuration change to an access switch.
ccna-200-301.question_text: How are the two interfaces in this scenario classified?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A northbound API sits between the controller and the applications or scripts above it; it is usually a REST API using JSON. A southbound API sits between the controller and the network devices below it; examples are NETCONF, RESTCONF, OpenFlow, OpFlex, SSH and SNMP. The direction is defined by position relative to the controller, not by the data format.

answers.answer_text: Script to controller: southbound; controller to switch: northbound
answers.rationale: The directions are reversed: applications sit north of the controller, devices south.

answers.answer_text: Both are northbound, because both carry structured data
answers.rationale: Direction depends on position relative to the controller, not on data format.

answers.answer_text: Script to controller: northbound; controller to switch: southbound
answers.rationale: Correct: the script consumes the controller REST API, and NETCONF programs the device.

answers.answer_text: Both are southbound, because each of them leads to a change on a device
answers.rationale: The script talks to the controller, not to a device, so its interface is northbound.

ccna-200-301.question_text: In a Cisco SD-Access fabric, user traffic between fabric edge nodes is encapsulated in VXLAN and carried across a routed network of physical switches and links. Which term describes the VXLAN tunnels?
ccna-200-301.explanation: An SD-Access fabric has two layers. The underlay is the physical network of switches and links running IP routing (typically IS-IS, as deployed by LAN Automation), which only needs reachability between fabric nodes. The overlay is the set of virtual networks built on top of it with VXLAN tunnels (LISP acts as its control plane), which carries user traffic and policy independently of the physical topology.

answers.answer_text: The overlay
answers.rationale: Correct: VXLAN tunnels create virtual networks on top of the physical network.

answers.answer_text: The underlay
answers.rationale: The underlay is the routed physical network that carries the VXLAN tunnels.

answers.answer_text: The management plane
answers.rationale: The management plane handles device access and configuration, not user traffic.

answers.answer_text: The southbound API
answers.rationale: A southbound API links the controller to devices; it does not carry user traffic.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which statement best describes the role of Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly Cisco DNA Center) in an enterprise network?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Catalyst Center is the controller for Cisco enterprise campus and branch networks. It provides automation (provisioning, software images, SD-Access fabric), assurance (monitoring and analytics) and policy. It exposes northbound REST APIs (the Intent API) to scripts and applications, and uses southbound protocols such as SSH, NETCONF and SNMP to manage devices. It is not in the data path: the switches still forward user traffic themselves.

answers.answer_text: It routes user traffic between VLANs in place of the distribution switches
answers.rationale: The controller is not in the data path; the switches still forward user traffic.

answers.answer_text: It is a hypervisor that hosts virtual routers on the campus switches
answers.rationale: Catalyst Center is a management and automation controller, not a hypervisor.

answers.answer_text: It disables the device CLI, so switches can no longer be configured locally
answers.rationale: Managed devices keep their CLI; the controller automates their configuration.

answers.answer_text: It is a controller that automates, manages and monitors campus devices
answers.rationale: Correct: it centralizes automation, assurance and policy, with northbound REST APIs.

ccna-200-301.topic: AI and machine learning in network operations
ccna-200-301.scenario: An engineer types into an AI assistant: "Summarize the interface errors seen on the core switches yesterday and draft a note for the incident ticket." The assistant replies with a written summary and a draft note.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which type of AI does this assistant represent?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Generative AI creates new content (text, summaries, configuration drafts) in response to a prompt, typically with a large language model. Predictive AI analyzes historical data to forecast or classify, for example predicting link saturation or detecting anomalies. In both cases the output supports the engineer, who still reviews it before acting.

answers.answer_text: Predictive AI, because it forecasts future interface errors
answers.rationale: The assistant summarizes past data and writes text; it does not forecast.

answers.answer_text: Generative AI, because it creates new text from a prompt
answers.rationale: Correct: producing a summary and a draft note from a prompt is generative AI.

answers.answer_text: Rule-based automation, because it runs a fixed script
answers.rationale: A fixed script does not interpret a free-text request or write new prose.

answers.answer_text: Traffic classification, because it labels packets by type
answers.rationale: Nothing here classifies packets; the assistant writes text in response to a prompt.

ccna-200-301.topic: AI and machine learning in network operations
ccna-200-301.question_text: How does machine-learning-based anomaly detection differ from a traditional static threshold alarm?
ccna-200-301.explanation: A static threshold triggers when a metric crosses a fixed value set by an administrator, whatever the context. Machine learning learns a baseline of normal behavior from telemetry (for example, high traffic is normal at 9 a.m. on Monday but not at 3 a.m.) and flags deviations from that baseline. This reduces false alarms and can reveal problems that stay under a fixed threshold.

answers.answer_text: It learns a baseline of normal behavior and flags deviations from it
answers.rationale: Correct: the model learns what is normal from data and detects departures from it.

answers.answer_text: It needs an administrator to enter a fixed limit for every metric
answers.rationale: Fixed, manually entered limits describe the static threshold approach.

answers.answer_text: It reacts to user complaints instead of analyzing telemetry data
answers.rationale: ML anomaly detection works from telemetry, to find issues before users report them.

answers.answer_text: It replaces telemetry collection with periodic manual CLI checks
answers.rationale: ML depends on collected data; manual CLI checks are the opposite approach.

ccna-200-301.question_text: A script must create a new resource through a REST API. Which HTTP method and success status code are expected?
ccna-200-301.explanation: REST maps CRUD operations to HTTP methods: Create = POST, Read = GET, Update = PUT (replace) or PATCH (partial change), Delete = DELETE. A successful creation typically returns 201 Created, a successful read 200 OK, and a successful delete often 204 No Content. Codes in the 4xx range indicate a client error, and 5xx a server error.

answers.answer_text: GET, with 200 OK
answers.rationale: GET reads an existing resource; it does not create one.

answers.answer_text: DELETE, with 204 No Content
answers.rationale: DELETE removes a resource; 204 is a common reply to a successful delete.

answers.answer_text: PATCH, with 400 Bad Request
answers.rationale: PATCH partially updates a resource, and 400 signals a malformed request, not success.

answers.answer_text: POST, with 201 Created
answers.rationale: Correct: POST maps to Create, and 201 confirms the resource was created.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
A script sends the request below. The token is valid, but the account it belongs to has read-only rights on the controller.

DELETE /api/v1/vlans/30 HTTP/1.1
Host: controller.example.com
X-Auth-Token: eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9...
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which HTTP status code is the controller most likely to return?
ccna-200-301.explanation: 401 Unauthorized means the client is not authenticated: credentials or token are missing, invalid or expired. 403 Forbidden means the client is authenticated but not allowed to perform this action on this resource. 404 Not Found means the URI does not match a resource, and 500 Internal Server Error means the server itself failed.

answers.answer_text: 401 Unauthorized
answers.rationale: 401 is for missing or invalid credentials; here the token is valid.

answers.answer_text: 403 Forbidden
answers.rationale: Correct: the client is authenticated but lacks permission to delete.

answers.answer_text: 404 Not Found
answers.rationale: Nothing suggests the VLAN 30 resource is missing; the issue is permissions.

answers.answer_text: 500 Internal Server Error
answers.rationale: 500 signals a server failure, not a refusal based on the client's rights.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
A script talks to a network controller with these requests:

1) POST /api/system/auth/token
   Authorization: Basic YWRtaW46Q2lzY28xMjM=
   Response: 200 OK {"Token": "eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1Qi..."}

2) GET /api/v1/network-device
   X-Auth-Token: eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1Qi...
ccna-200-301.question_text: Which authentication method does request 2 use?
ccna-200-301.explanation: With token-based authentication, the client first authenticates once (here with Basic credentials) and receives a token, usually with an expiry time. It then sends that token in a header with each following request, so the username and password are not repeated. An API key is a static secret issued in advance, and Basic authentication sends the Base64-encoded username and password on every request.

answers.answer_text: HTTP Basic authentication, with credentials sent on each request
answers.rationale: Basic is used once in request 1; request 2 carries no Authorization: Basic header.

answers.answer_text: A static API key issued in advance by an administrator
answers.rationale: The value was obtained from a login request just before, not issued in advance.

answers.answer_text: Token-based authentication with a token from a login request
answers.rationale: Correct: request 1 returns a token that request 2 sends in X-Auth-Token.

answers.answer_text: Certificate-based authentication with mutual TLS
answers.rationale: Nothing in the requests shows a client certificate; the header carries a token.

ccna-200-301.scenario:
An engineer runs this playbook from an Ansible control node:

- name: Configure NTP on branch routers
  hosts: branch_routers
  gather_facts: no
  tasks:
    - name: Set NTP server
      cisco.ios.ios_config:
        lines:
          - ntp server 10.0.0.10
ccna-200-301.question_text: How does Ansible apply this playbook to the routers?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Ansible is agentless and uses a push model: the control node reads the YAML playbook and the inventory, connects to each device (over SSH for Cisco IOS), and applies the tasks. Nothing needs to be installed on the routers. This differs from agent-based tools that pull configuration from a server, and from Terraform, which uses HCL files and a state file.

answers.answer_text: An agent installed on each router pulls the playbook from a server every 30 minutes
answers.rationale: Ansible is agentless and pushes changes; it does not rely on a pull agent.

answers.answer_text: Each router downloads the playbook from a TFTP server when it boots
answers.rationale: Routers do not read Ansible playbooks; the control node runs them.

answers.answer_text: Terraform converts the YAML playbook into HCL before applying it
answers.rationale: Ansible and Terraform are separate tools; Ansible runs its playbooks itself.

answers.answer_text: The control node pushes the tasks over SSH, with no agent on the routers
answers.rationale: Correct: Ansible is agentless and pushes changes from the control node over SSH.

ccna-200-301.scenario: An engineer describes network resources in .tf files written in HCL. Before applying a change, she runs terraform plan, and Terraform compares the desired configuration with the resources it recorded during the last terraform apply.
ccna-200-301.question_text: Where does Terraform keep the record of the resources it manages?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Terraform is declarative: HCL files describe the desired end state, and providers translate that into API calls for each platform. Terraform keeps a state file (terraform.tfstate by default) that maps the configuration to the real resources. terraform plan compares the desired configuration, the state and the real infrastructure to show what will be created, changed or destroyed before terraform apply runs.

answers.answer_text: In a YAML playbook stored on the Ansible control node
answers.rationale: YAML playbooks belong to Ansible, which does not keep a state file.

answers.answer_text: In the startup-config of each managed device
answers.rationale: Terraform does not store its records on the managed devices.

answers.answer_text: In a state file, terraform.tfstate by default
answers.rationale: Correct: the state file maps the HCL configuration to the real resources.

answers.answer_text: In an inventory file listing the SSH hosts
answers.rationale: An inventory of SSH hosts is an Ansible concept, not Terraform state.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which snippet is valid JSON?
ccna-200-301.explanation: In JSON, an object is enclosed in curly braces and contains key/value pairs separated by commas, with a colon between each key and its value. Keys and string values use double quotes, never single quotes. Arrays use square brackets, and a trailing comma after the last element is not allowed.

answers.answer_text: {"hostname": "R1", "interfaces": ["Gi0/0", "Gi0/1"]}
answers.rationale: Correct: double-quoted keys and strings, colons, commas and a proper array.

answers.answer_text: {'hostname': 'R1', 'interfaces': ['Gi0/0', 'Gi0/1']}
answers.rationale: JSON requires double quotes; single quotes make this invalid.

answers.answer_text: {"hostname": "R1", "interfaces": ["Gi0/0", "Gi0/1"],}
answers.rationale: The trailing comma before the closing brace is not allowed in JSON.

answers.answer_text: {"hostname" = "R1", "interfaces" = ["Gi0/0", "Gi0/1"]}
answers.rationale: JSON separates a key from its value with a colon, not an equals sign.

ccna-200-301.question_text: Which statement correctly describes the value of the "vlans" key?
ccna-200-301.explanation: Square brackets enclose a JSON array (an ordered list of values), and curly braces enclose an object (a set of key/value pairs). Here "vlans" is an array of two objects, each with the keys "id" (a number) and "name" (a string). The other top-level values are a string ("SW1") and a boolean (true, written without quotes).

answers.answer_text: An object whose keys are the VLAN numbers 10 and 20
answers.rationale: The value starts with a square bracket, so it is an array; 10 and 20 are values of "id".

answers.answer_text: An array of two objects, each with two key/value pairs
answers.rationale: Correct: square brackets hold two objects, each with "id" and "name".

answers.answer_text: A string that lists two VLAN names separated by a comma
answers.rationale: A string would be one double-quoted value, not brackets containing objects.

answers.answer_text: A boolean set to true, because the switch is managed
answers.rationale: true is the value of "managed", a different key.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une équipe informatique livre une nouvelle application dans les délais et respecte toutes les spécifications. Pourtant, les utilisateurs mettent davantage de temps à accomplir leur travail qu’avec l’ancienne application.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle affirmation est la plus correcte ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: ITIL distingue soigneusement une sortie (output - livrable tangible ou intangible d'une activité) d'un résultat (outcome - ce que la partie prenante retire de cette sortie). Ici, l'application (sortie) est livrée, mais l'outcome attendu (productivité utilisateur) n'est pas au rendez-vous.

answers.answer_text: La valeur a été co-créée puisque les spécifications et délais convenus ont été respectés
answers.rationale: Respecter les spécifications et les délais produit une sortie ; la valeur dépend du résultat obtenu par les utilisateurs.

answers.answer_text: Une sortie a été livrée, mais le résultat attendu n’a probablement pas été atteint
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte de la distinction sortie/résultat : la sortie est là, le résultat attendu ne l'est pas.

answers.answer_text: Le résultat a été atteint, mais la garantie de l'application est insuffisante
answers.rationale: Les utilisateurs sont plus lents : le résultat n'est pas atteint, et rien n'indique un problème de garantie.

answers.answer_text: L'application manque de garantie, il faut donc augmenter sa capacité et sa disponibilité
answers.rationale: Rien n'indique un problème de capacité ou de disponibilité ; l'écart se situe entre la sortie et le résultat.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une entreprise réduit le prix d’un service, mais augmente fortement les délais de résolution. Certains clients restent satisfaits, tandis que d’autres considèrent le service inutilisable.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Que montre principalement cette situation ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: ITIL définit la valeur comme quelque chose de perçu - elle dépend des attentes, du contexte et du rôle de chaque partie prenante. C'est un pilier du système de valeur ITIL.

answers.answer_text: La valeur est définie par le fournisseur en fonction du coût du service
answers.rationale: La valeur est jugée par les parties prenantes, pas fixée par le fournisseur à partir de ses coûts.

answers.answer_text: La valeur dépend principalement du prix facturé pour le service
answers.rationale: Le prix n'est qu'un élément de coût ; les délais de résolution (garantie) influencent aussi la valeur perçue.

answers.answer_text: La valeur est perçue différemment selon les parties prenantes et leur contexte
answers.rationale: La valeur est perçue : selon leur contexte, certains clients privilégient le prix, d'autres la rapidité.

answers.answer_text: La valeur se limite à l'utilité, le délai de résolution n'a donc pas d'effet
answers.rationale: Le délai de résolution relève de la garantie, qui contribue aussi à la valeur.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Un fournisseur met à disposition une plateforme cloud, tandis que le client reste responsable de la configuration des comptes utilisateurs et de la sécurité de ses données.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel concept cette situation illustre-t-elle le mieux ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: ITIL 4 remplace le modèle « fournisseur produit → client consomme » par la co-création : les deux parties participent activement à la production de valeur, chacune gardant certaines responsabilités et certains risques.

answers.answer_text: La valeur est créée par le fournisseur puis livrée au consommateur
answers.rationale: ITIL décrit une co-création de valeur, pas une livraison à sens unique.

answers.answer_text: Le consommateur participe aussi à la création de valeur et à la gestion des risques
answers.rationale: Le client configure les comptes et sécurise ses données : il co-crée la valeur et partage la gestion des risques.

answers.answer_text: Les risques sont transférés au fournisseur grâce au contrat de service cloud souscrit
answers.rationale: Le client garde des risques sur les comptes et les données ; un service retire certains risques et en impose d'autres.

answers.answer_text: Il s'agit d'un transfert de biens, la propriété passe donc au client
answers.rationale: Le fournisseur garde la propriété de la plateforme : il s'agit d'un accès à des ressources.

itil-foundation-v5.topic: Principe - Commencer là où vous êtes
itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une organisation prévoit de remplacer son outil de gestion des tickets. Avant de le faire, elle analyse l’outil actuel et découvre que la plupart des problèmes viennent d’une mauvaise configuration.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel principe directeur est principalement appliqué ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Start where you are » invite à évaluer l'existant (outils, données, processus, compétences) avant toute refonte. On peut réutiliser beaucoup plus qu'on ne le pense - c'est ce que l'organisation fait ici en analysant la config avant de racheter.

answers.answer_text: Commencer là où vous êtes
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte du principe qui recommande d'auditer l'existant plutôt que de repartir de zéro.

answers.answer_text: Privilégier la valeur
answers.rationale: « Focus on value » cible la finalité (utilité pour le consommateur), pas la posture d'analyse initiale de l'existant.

answers.answer_text: Collaborer et promouvoir la visibilité
answers.rationale: « Collaborate and promote visibility » porte sur les échanges entre équipes et la transparence, pas sur l'audit de l'outil.

answers.answer_text: Progresser par itérations avec des retours
answers.rationale: « Progress iteratively » traite du rythme du changement (petits pas + feedback), pas du diagnostic de départ.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une équipe automatise un processus comportant douze validations. Le processus automatisé reste lent, car dix validations n’apportent aucune valeur.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle approche aurait été la plus appropriée ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: Le principe « Optimize and automate » impose un ordre strict : d'abord optimiser (supprimer le gaspillage, simplifier), puis seulement automatiser. Automatiser un mauvais processus = obtenir un mauvais processus plus rapidement.

answers.answer_text: Automatiser d’abord, puis analyser le processus après plusieurs années
answers.rationale: Inverse la bonne séquence - cela conserve les validations inutiles et gaspille du temps d'automatisation.

answers.answer_text: Optimiser le processus avant de l’automatiser
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte du principe. Retirer les 10 validations sans valeur d'abord aurait fait gagner du temps réel.

answers.answer_text: Ajouter davantage de validations automatisées
answers.rationale: Aggrave le problème initial (excès de validations) au lieu de le corriger.

answers.answer_text: Transférer le processus à une autre équipe
answers.rationale: Ne résout rien - déplacer un mauvais processus vers une autre équipe ne l'optimise pas.

itil-foundation-v5.topic: Principe - Penser et travailler de manière holistique
itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une amélioration réduit le temps de traitement du service desk, mais augmente considérablement la charge des équipes réseau et sécurité.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel principe directeur a principalement été négligé ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Think and work holistically » demande de considérer l'ensemble du système de valeur et ses dépendances avant de changer une partie. Optimiser un maillon isolément déplace souvent le problème ailleurs - c'est ce qui s'est passé ici.

answers.answer_text: Faire simple et pratique
answers.rationale: Ce principe concerne la simplicité des solutions, pas la vision d'ensemble des impacts.

answers.answer_text: Commencer là où vous êtes
answers.rationale: Ce principe concerne l'audit de l'existant, pas la vision transverse des dépendances entre équipes.

answers.answer_text: Penser et travailler de manière holistique
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte : ne pas penser au système entier a fait exploser la charge réseau et sécurité.

answers.answer_text: Progresser par itérations avec des retours
answers.rationale: Ce principe porte sur le rythme du changement (petites itérations), pas sur la couverture transverse des dépendances.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Un projet de six mois est divisé en livraisons de deux semaines. Après chaque livraison, les utilisateurs donnent leur avis et les priorités sont ajustées.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel principe est principalement appliqué ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Progress iteratively with feedback » recommande de découper un chantier en petits incréments livrés régulièrement, avec retour utilisateur entre chaque, pour ajuster la trajectoire.

answers.answer_text: Privilégier la valeur
answers.rationale: « Focus on value » cible la finalité perçue par le consommateur, pas le rythme de livraison.

answers.answer_text: Progresser par itérations avec des retours
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte du principe - livraisons de 2 semaines + feedback + réajustement des priorités.

answers.answer_text: Optimiser et automatiser
answers.rationale: « Optimize and automate » traite d'amélioration de processus, pas de découpage projet.

answers.answer_text: Faire simple et pratique
answers.rationale: « Keep it simple and practical » porte sur la sobriété des solutions, pas sur la boucle de feedback itérative.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une équipe produit chaque semaine un rapport de 80 pages. Seules deux pages sont réellement utilisées pour prendre des décisions.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle action correspond le mieux au principe « Faire simple et pratique » ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Keep it simple and practical » demande d'éliminer ce qui n'apporte pas de valeur. Attention : la démarche reste pragmatique - on garde ce qui sert, on retire ce qui encombre, sans jeter le bébé avec l'eau du bain.

answers.answer_text: Ajouter davantage de données au rapport
answers.rationale: Aggrave le problème : plus de bruit, moins de signal.

answers.answer_text: Supprimer le rapport sans consulter les utilisateurs
answers.rationale: Supprimer sans consulter viole le principe de collaboration et risque de retirer les 2 pages utiles.

answers.answer_text: Conserver les informations utiles et supprimer la complexité inutile
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte : garder l'utile, retirer le superflu - c'est la posture « simple et pratique » en action.

answers.answer_text: Automatiser la production des 80 pages sans modifier leur contenu
answers.rationale: Automatise du gaspillage - on produit plus vite un rapport dont personne ne se sert. Contraire à l'esprit du principe.

itil-foundation-v5.topic: Principe - Collaborer et promouvoir la visibilité
itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une organisation veut améliorer l’onboarding informatique. Elle réunit les ressources humaines, le service desk, la sécurité et les managers afin de rendre visibles les dépendances et responsabilités.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel principe est principalement appliqué ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Collaborate and promote visibility » demande d'impliquer toutes les parties concernées ET de rendre transparent ce qu'on fait (dashboard, mapping des rôles). C'est exactement l'atelier multi-équipes décrit.

answers.answer_text: Collaborer et promouvoir la visibilité
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte du principe : équipes croisées + visibilité des dépendances = collaboration transparente.

answers.answer_text: Commencer là où vous êtes
answers.rationale: « Start where you are » = auditer l'existant. Ici, on organise la coopération, pas l'audit.

answers.answer_text: Faire simple et pratique
answers.rationale: « Keep it simple » cible la sobriété, pas la collaboration multi-équipes.

answers.answer_text: Optimiser et automatiser
answers.rationale: « Optimize and automate » vient plus tard, une fois la collaboration établie et le processus compris.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Avant de modifier un service, une équipe demande : « Quel bénéfice concret les utilisateurs et l’organisation doivent-ils obtenir ? »
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quel principe applique-t-elle principalement ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: « Focus on value » impose de partir de la valeur attendue (utilité et bénéfice pour le consommateur/organisation) avant toute décision. La question posée est le déclencheur type de ce principe.

answers.answer_text: Penser et travailler de manière holistique
answers.rationale: « Think holistically » concerne les impacts transverses, pas la finalité recherchée.

answers.answer_text: Privilégier la valeur
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte - chercher le bénéfice concret pour utilisateur et organisation, c'est la définition du principe.

answers.answer_text: Commencer là où vous êtes
answers.rationale: « Start where you are » = audit de l'existant, pas définition de l'objectif.

answers.answer_text: Progresser par itérations avec des retours
answers.rationale: « Progress iteratively » = rythme, pas cible.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une entreprise étudie les compétences requises, les responsabilités, la culture et la résistance au changement avant de déployer un nouvel outil.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle dimension est principalement concernée ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: La dimension « Organizations and people » couvre les rôles, responsabilités, structures organisationnelles, compétences, cultures et posture face au changement. C'est exactement ce que l'entreprise analyse.

answers.answer_text: Information et technologie
answers.rationale: « Information and technology » vise données, applis, infrastructures et cybersécurité, pas les compétences humaines.

answers.answer_text: Organisations et personnes
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte : compétences + culture + responsabilités = dimension humaine et organisationnelle.

answers.answer_text: Partenaires et fournisseurs
answers.rationale: « Partners and suppliers » traite des relations contractuelles externes.

answers.answer_text: Flux de valeur et processus
answers.rationale: « Value streams and processes » cartographie les activités, pas les compétences.

itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une organisation évalue la qualité des données, les intégrations, les infrastructures et la cybersécurité d’une solution.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle dimension est principalement concernée ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: La dimension « Information and technology » englobe qualité des données, intégrations, infras, sécurité et technologies utilisées pour délivrer le service. Description textuelle du périmètre.

answers.answer_text: Organisations et personnes
answers.rationale: « Organizations and people » concerne les humains et structures, pas les infrastructures.

answers.answer_text: Partenaires et fournisseurs
answers.rationale: « Partners and suppliers » porte sur les relations externes, pas les intégrations techniques internes.

answers.answer_text: Information et technologie
answers.rationale: Formulation exacte : données + intégrations + infra + cybersécurité = dimension IT.

answers.answer_text: Flux de valeur et processus
answers.rationale: « Value streams and processes » cartographie les flux de travail, pas la tech sous-jacente.

itil-foundation-v5.topic: Dimension - Flux de valeur et processus
itil-foundation-v5.scenario: Une entreprise analyse les activités, transferts, délais d’attente et blocages nécessaires pour répondre à une demande utilisateur.
itil-foundation-v5.question_text: Quelle dimension est principalement concernée ?
itil-foundation-v5.explanation: La dimension « Value streams and processes » cartographie la séquence d'activités, transferts, délais et blocages qui transforment une demande en valeur livrée. C'est la vue « comment le travail circule ».
